title: The Tower of Cindral
summary: A vertical level designed to teach the double jump without a single text tutorial.

sections.heading: The Challenge
sections.text: Teach the double jump without breaking the pacing of vertical exploration or relying on a tutorial popup.

sections.heading: The Solution
sections.text: A first guiding platform forces the short jump; the gap to the second one only closes with a double jump, read through silhouette rather than text. Three greybox iterations before moving to final art.

sections.heading: Result
sections.text: In playtesting, 9 out of 10 players found the double jump on their own on the first attempt, without pausing or opening the help menu.

title: Shelter 09
summary: Combat design in tight spaces focused on managing limited resources.

sections.heading: The Challenge
sections.text: Make a cramped interior feel tense rather than cramped, while keeping the player's limited ammo count readable at a glance.

sections.heading: The Solution
sections.text: Encounters are staged around sightlines instead of enemy count — fewer enemies, more angles. Resource pickups are placed to reward exploration over hoarding.

sections.heading: Result
sections.text: Average ammo usage across playtests dropped by 30% once pickups were repositioned, without reducing perceived difficulty.

title: Dry Basin
summary: Non-linear exploration using environmental signposting instead of maps or markers.

sections.heading: The Challenge
sections.text: Guide players across a large open basin without a minimap, quest markers, or compass.

sections.heading: The Solution
sections.text: Landmarks are placed on a readable skyline, and erosion patterns in the terrain itself hint at the route to water.

sections.heading: Result
sections.text: Players reached the first landmark in under four minutes on average, with no verbal or UI guidance.

title: Last Train
summary: A linear sequence building tension through encounter pacing and lighting.

sections.heading: The Challenge
sections.text: Build dread across a ten-minute linear sequence without repeating the same scare twice.

sections.heading: The Solution
sections.text: Three escalating encounter types are interleaved with quiet beats, and lighting gradually narrows the player's field of safety.

sections.heading: Result
sections.text: Heart-rate data from playtests showed a steady climb across the sequence rather than isolated spikes.

title: Inner Courtyard
summary: A co-op puzzle prototype tested with two players on the same screen.

sections.heading: The Challenge
sections.text: Design puzzles that require real communication between two players sharing one screen, not just parallel button-pressing.

sections.heading: The Solution
sections.text: Each player sees information the other cannot, forcing them to describe what they see out loud to solve each room.

sections.heading: Result
sections.text: Every tested pair solved the final room through conversation alone, with no shared visual confirmation.

title: Block Zero
summary: A greybox level iterated twelve times based on playtest data.

sections.heading: The Challenge
sections.text: Validate a core traversal loop before committing any art budget to the level.

sections.heading: The Solution
sections.text: Twelve greybox passes, each changing one variable — sightline height, jump distance, or checkpoint spacing — tested with the same five players.

sections.heading: Result
sections.text: Completion time variance across testers dropped from 6 minutes to under 90 seconds by the final pass.
